--- title: "JupyterLab" jupyter: php --- ## Starting a notebook Start JupyterLab from the Python environment that has it: ```bash ~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/jupyter lab ``` The launcher lists each kernel juphyter registered under its display name, such as "PHP 8.5" for the default `php` kernel and "PHP (phpstats)" for the kernel from [Installation](install.qmd#the-phpstats-packages). A notebook that is already open changes kernel through **Kernel > Change Kernel**. JupyterLab finds kernels in the per-user Jupyter data directory and in `JUPYTER_DATA_DIR` when it is set. `jupyter kernelspec list` shows the kernels a JupyterLab started from the same environment will find. ## Running cells A cell's result appears under it as `Out[n]`. State carries from one cell to the next. The stop button interrupts a running cell when PHP has the `pcntl` extension, and **Kernel > Restart Kernel** starts a new PHP session with nothing defined. Tab completion covers three cases: - Variables in the session, after a `$`. - Declared functions and classes, for a bare prefix. - Public methods, properties, and constants, after `->` or `::`. An unfinished block or string keeps the cell open for another line instead of running it. ## Project classes Jupyter starts the kernel in the notebook's directory. The kernel looks upward from there for `vendor/autoload.php`, so a notebook saved inside a Composer project can use that project's classes and packages. A notebook kept outside the project it works on names the autoloader in a `juphyter.json` beside it: ```json { "autoload": "../app/vendor/autoload.php" } ``` [Which classes a notebook sees](install.qmd#which-classes-a-notebook-sees) lists every way to set it. ## Tables A phibble data frame appears as an HTML table with its dimensions and column types. The table's styles use JupyterLab's theme variables, so it follows the light and dark themes. ::: {#9c5d0624 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.php .cell-code} DataFrame::fromRows([ ['front end' => 'JupyterLab', 'plot from' => 'the Vega-Lite spec', 'table from' => 'text/html'], ['front end' => 'Quarto HTML', 'plot from' => 'the HTML embed', 'table from' => 'text/html'], ['front end' => 'Quarto PDF', 'plot from' => 'the static SVG', 'table from' => 'the parsed table'], ]); ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
A tibble: 3 × 3
front end <chr>plot from <chr>table from <chr>
1JupyterLabthe Vega-Lite spectext/html
2Quarto HTMLthe HTML embedtext/html
3Quarto PDFthe static SVGthe parsed table
``` ::: ::: ## Plots JupyterLab draws a phiz plot from its Vega-Lite specification and needs no extension for it. phiz writes Vega-Lite 6 specifications, and juphyter publishes them under `application/vnd.vegalite.v5+json`, the newest Vega-Lite type JupyterLab's built-in renderer accepts. On 2026-10-19, with phiz 0.3, JupyterLab's bundled Vega-Lite 5.6.1 compiled all sixteen phiz specifications tested. juphyter also publishes a static SVG and an HTML version of each plot. JupyterLab uses neither. It does not run scripts in HTML output, and the HTML version is a container with a script that draws the chart, so it would show as an empty box. The SVG serves Quarto's PDF and Word output, front ends without JavaScript, and any Vega-Lite 6 construct that the version 5 renderer rejects. ## Converting a notebook `quarto convert` turns a `.ipynb` into a `.qmd` and back, and `jupyter nbconvert` exports a notebook to HTML or PDF. Both work on a PHP notebook, because they read the notebook file format and not the language.
